titel: There’s a quick way to slow climate change. Why isn’t everyone doing it?

einzeiler: Turkmenistan takes action on massive methane leaks after Guardian reporting.
kurzfassung: Satellites have exposed massive methane mega-leaks around the world, which experts call a crucial climate emergency break. After Guardian reporting revealed Turkmenistan's staggering emissions, the authoritarian nation began cooperating with the UN to plug leaks. While other major emitters like the US stall under political changes, several countries are showing progress in fixing their infrastructure.
stichpunkte: Methane traps 80 times more heat than carbon dioxide and accounts for 25% of global warming.
Satellites launched in recent years have enabled researchers to spot over a thousand methane mega-leaks globally.
Fixing leaky pipes and valves offers a rapid way to slow global heating, earning methane cuts the label of climate emergency break.
Turkmenistan's methane emissions from just two gas fields matched the entire greenhouse gas output of the United Kingdom.
International reporting and UN monitoring pressure pushed Ashgabat to engage and plug initial leaks.
The UN-backed Methane Alert and Response System uses AI and satellites to notify governments and track repairs.
While the US under a new administration has halted engagement, countries like Kazakhstan, Oman, and Argentina have successfully repaired leaks.

clips.text: Rapidly reducing global heating is possible by addressing faulty infrastructure because the gas leaves the atmosphere quickly.
Two specific gas fields in an authoritarian republic produced greenhouse gas quantities equivalent to the total output of the United Kingdom.

clips.hook: Fixing leaks can be surprisingly simple
clips.text: Stopping some emissions requires nothing more than visiting the site with basic tools and tightening a few mechanical parts.

clips.hook: A sudden halt in the United States
clips.text: The second largest emitter stopped responding to international alerts and completely abandoned cooperation following a political transition.

clips.hook: Shouting into the wind in environmental journalism
clips.text: Covering ecological crises often feels like an isolated effort with little hope of ever seeing tangible real-world consequences.

beschreibung: Methane is a potent greenhouse gas that traps more than 80 times as much heat than carbon dioxide over a 20-year period and causes 25% of global heating today. We definitely don’t want this gas spewing needlessly into the atmosphere, but in 2023 that’s exactly what environment editor Damian Carrington found was happening when he reported on 1,000 super-emitting methane leaks across the globe. Now Turkmenistan, the worst country for mega-leaks, has begun to plug them. Damian tells Madeleine Finlay why some experts call stopping leaks the climate ‘emergency brake’ and reveals which countries are still failing to act.
